stem.es: Un crayón empieza en el extremo 0 de una regla de cubos y termina en la marca 8. ¿Cuántos cubos mide?

hints.en: Start counting at the 0 end.
Count each cube space until the crayon ends.
The number where it ends tells the length.

steps: The crayon starts at 0 and ends at 8.
solution.es: Empieza en 0 y termina en 8: mide 8 cubos.

objective: Compose a three-dimensional shape from cubes and count the cubes.

stem.en: Mia builds one stack with 3 cubes and another stack with 4 cubes. How many cubes are in the two stacks?
stem.es: Mia construye una torre con 3 cubos y otra torre con 4 cubos. ¿Cuántos cubos hay en las dos torres?

hints.en: Count the cubes in both stacks.
Put the two stacks together.
Count on 4 from 3.

steps: The cubes in both stacks are added.

objective: Subtract from ten using a known fact.

stem.en: A tray holds 10 cups. 7 cups are blue and the rest are green. How many cups are green?
stem.es: Una bandeja tiene 10 vasos. 7 vasos son azules y el resto son verdes. ¿Cuántos vasos son verdes?

hints.en: Ten is the whole tray.
Take away the blue cups.
Think: 7 and how many more make ten?

steps: The whole is 10 and the blue part is 7.

objective: Name the parts when a shape is cut into 2 equal shares.

stem.en: A sandwich is cut into 2 equal parts. What do we call each part?
stem.es: Un sándwich se corta en 2 partes iguales. ¿Cómo se llama cada parte?

choices.why: A fourth is one of 4 equal parts. Here there are only 2.
A whole is the sandwich before it is cut.
A third is one of 3 equal parts. Here there are 2.

hints.en: Count how many equal parts there are.
The name depends on the number of equal parts.
Two equal parts have a special name.

solution.es: Son 2 partes iguales: cada parte es una mitad.

objective: Sort ways of cutting a shape into halves or fourths.

stem.en: Sort each way of cutting a shape: does it make halves or fourths?
stem.es: Clasifica cada forma de cortar una figura: ¿hace mitades o cuartos?

items.es: Un corte a lo ancho por el medio

items.en: Cut in half, then cut each half in half
items.es: Cortar por la mitad y luego cortar cada mitad por la mitad

items.en: Cut down the middle and across the middle
items.es: Un corte vertical y uno horizontal por el medio

hints.en: Count how many equal parts you get.
One cut makes 2 parts.
Cutting each half again makes more parts.

steps: One cut makes 2 equal parts, which are halves.
Cutting each half in half makes 2 × 2 = 4 parts, which are fourths.
solution.es: Un corte da 2 mitades; cortar cada mitad otra vez da 4 cuartos.

objective: Find the step that gives a tens digit the value of ones.

stem.en: Tim looks at 83. Which step of his thinking has the mistake?
stem.es: Tim mira el 83. ¿Qué paso de su razonamiento tiene el error?

steps: The 8 is in the tens place.

hints.en: A digit's place tells its value.
Look at what the tens place means.
Is the 8 worth 8 ones or 8 tens?

steps: The 8 is in the tens place, so it is worth 8 tens.

objective: Find the step that adds when a comparison needs subtraction.

stem.en: A chart shows dogs 9 and cats 4. Zia says there are 13 more dogs than cats. Which step is wrong?
stem.es: Una tabla muestra perros 9 y gatos 4. Zia dice que hay 13 perros más que gatos. ¿Qué paso está mal?

steps: The chart shows dogs 9 and cats 4.
To find how many more, compare the two numbers.

hints.en: How many more means finding the difference.
Does adding the two numbers show how many more?
Think: 4 plus what number makes 9?

steps: To find how many more, subtract.
solution.es: Para saber cuántos más, se resta: 9 − 4 = 5 perros más.

objective: Critique and correct a near-doubles argument.

stem.en: Pia says 8 + 7 = 14 because 7 + 7 = 14. Is she right? Explain how to fix her thinking.
stem.es: Pia dice que 8 + 7 = 14 porque 7 + 7 = 14. ¿Tiene razón? Explica cómo corregir su razonamiento.

criteria.en: Explains 8 is one more than 7, so the total is one more than 14
criteria.es: Explica que 8 es uno más que 7, así que el total es uno más que 14

sample.en: No. 7 + 7 = 14, but 8 is one more than 7, so 8 + 7 is one more than 14. 8 + 7 = 15.
sample.es: No. 7 + 7 = 14, pero 8 es uno más que 7, así que 8 + 7 es uno más que 14. 8 + 7 = 15.

hints.en: Compare 8 + 7 with the double 7 + 7.
Is the 8 the same as 7, or is it different?
Think about how much more or less 8 is than 7.

solution.es: 8 es uno más que 7, así que 8 + 7 = 14 + 1 = 15.

objective: Use a doubles fact to add near doubles.

stem.en: Use the double 6 + 6 to help solve 6 + 7. What is 6 + 7?
stem.es: Usa el doble 6 + 6 para resolver 6 + 7. ¿Cuánto es 6 + 7?

choices.why: That is the double 6 + 6. The 7 is one more than 6.
That is 7 + 7. One of the numbers here is 6.
That writes the digits side by side. Add the numbers.

hints.en: You know 6 + 6 is a double.
7 is one more than 6.
Add one more to the double.

objective: Solve a take-from story with the change unknown.

stem.en: A pond had 15 ducks. Some swam away. Now 8 ducks are left. How many ducks swam away?
stem.es: Un estanque tenía 15 patos. Algunos se fueron nadando. Ahora quedan 8 patos. ¿Cuántos patos se fueron?

sample.en: 8 + 7 = 15, so 7 ducks swam away.
sample.es: 8 + 7 = 15, así que se fueron 7 patos.

hints.en: Some ducks left, so there are fewer now.
The ducks that stayed and the ducks that left make 15.
Think: 8 plus what number makes 15?

objective: Choose an order of addends that makes a ten.

stem.en: Zara has 5 red, 8 blue and 5 yellow balloons. Which two groups are easiest to add first?
stem.es: Zara tiene 5 globos rojos, 8 azules y 5 amarillos. ¿Cuáles dos grupos son más fáciles de sumar primero?

choices.why: 5 + 8 makes 13, not a ten. Look for two groups that make 10.
8 + 5 makes 13, not a ten.

hints.en: Look for two groups that fit together to make a ten.
Which two numbers are the same?
Add those two groups first, then add the third.

objective: Explain why an equation with additions on both sides is true.

stem.en: Is 6 + 4 = 5 + 5 true? How do you know?
stem.es: ¿Es verdadera 6 + 4 = 5 + 5? ¿Cómo lo sabes?

criteria.es: Halla que los dos lados son 10

sample.en: Yes, it is true. 6 + 4 = 10 and 5 + 5 = 10, so both sides are the same amount.
sample.es: Sí, es verdadera. 6 + 4 = 10 y 5 + 5 = 10, así que los dos lados valen lo mismo.

hints.en: Add the numbers on the left side.
Add the numbers on the right side.
Compare the two totals.

steps: Both sides are 10, so it is true.
solution.es: Los dos lados valen 10, así que es verdadera.

objective: Find the step that treats the equal sign as 'the answer comes next'.

stem.en: Lia says 4 + 3 = 7 + 2 is true. Which step of her thinking is wrong?
stem.es: Lia dice que 4 + 3 = 7 + 2 es verdadera. ¿Qué paso de su razonamiento está mal?

steps: The equal sign means the answer comes next.

hints.en: Work out both sides of the equation.
Is 7 the same amount as 7 + 2?
The equal sign compares the two sides.

steps: The equal sign means both sides are the same amount.
4 + 3 = 7 but 7 + 2 = 9, so the equation is false.
solution.es: 4 + 3 = 7 y 7 + 2 = 9. Los lados no son iguales, la ecuación es falsa.

objective: Understand the equal sign as meaning the same amount.

stem.en: In 6 = 4 + 2, what does the equal sign tell us?
stem.es: En 6 = 4 + 2, ¿qué nos dice el signo igual?

choices.why: Here the 6 comes first. There is no answer after the equal sign.

text.en: Add the numbers on the right.
text.es: Add the numbers on the right.

choices.why: Adding is done by the plus sign. The equal sign compares the sides.
Bigger or smaller would use a different symbol. Equal means the same.

text.en: Both sides are the same amount.
text.es: Both sides are the same amount.

hints.en: Look at both sides of the equal sign.
Work out 4 + 2.
Compare 4 + 2 with the 6.

steps: The equal sign says both sides have the same amount.
solution.es: 4 + 2 = 6. El signo igual dice que los dos lados valen lo mismo.

verify.note: This asks for the meaning of the equal sign in words; no computation can prove it, so a person should review the wording.

objective: Identify sums within 100 that equal a target.

stem.en: Select ALL the sums that equal 65.
stem.es: Selecciona TODAS las sumas que son iguales a 65.

choices.why: 55 + 5 is 60. It is 5 short of 65.
62 + 4 is 66, one more than 65.

hints.en: Work out each sum with tens and ones.
Add the tens first, then the ones.
Three sums make 65 and two do not.

objective: Identify equations whose unknown number has the same value.

stem.en: Select ALL the equations where n = 6.
stem.es: Selecciona TODAS las ecuaciones donde n = 6.

choices.why: For n + 7 = 12, n is 5. Check: 5 + 7 = 12.
For 14 − n = 9, n is 5. Check: 14 − 5 = 9.

hints.en: Put 6 in place of n in each equation.
Check whether both sides are the same amount.
Three equations work and two do not.

solution.es: Con n = 6 se cumplen n+4=10, 9−n=3 y n−2=4.

objective: Choose the number sentence that belongs to a fact family.

stem.en: Which number sentence uses the numbers 3, 8 and 11 as a fact family?
stem.es: ¿Qué oración numérica usa los números 3, 8 y 11 como una familia de operaciones?

choices.why: The biggest number is the total, so 11 should be the answer to the addition.
8 − 3 is 5. In subtraction the total, 11, comes first.
11 + 8 is much bigger than 3.

hints.en: In a fact family the biggest number is the total.
The two smaller numbers are the parts.
Parts added together make the total.

steps: The total is 11 and the parts are 3 and 8.
solution.es: El total es 11 y las partes son 3 y 8: 3 + 8 = 11.

objective: Identify addition facts with a sum of ten.

stem.en: Select ALL the facts that make 10.
stem.es: Selecciona TODAS las sumas que dan 10.

choices.why: 7 + 2 is 9, which is one less than 10.
9 + 2 is 11, which is one more than 10.

hints.en: Add each pair of numbers.
Think about how many more each number needs to reach ten.
Three facts make 10 and two do not.

objective: Use a data total to find the missing category.

stem.en: Sam asks 14 children their favorite color. 6 choose red and 5 choose blue. The rest choose green. How many choose green?
stem.es: Sam pregunta a 14 niños cuál es su color favorito. 6 eligen rojo y 5 eligen azul. El resto elige verde. ¿Cuántos eligen verde?

criteria.en: Adds or subtracts to account for red and blue
criteria.es: Suma o resta para tener en cuenta rojo y azul

sample.en: 6 + 5 = 11 chose red or blue. 14 − 11 = 3 chose green.
sample.es: 6 + 5 = 11 eligieron rojo o azul. 14 − 11 = 3 eligieron verde.

hints.en: All the children are in one of three groups.
Find how many chose red or blue together.
Take that number away from the total.

objective: Solve a compare problem that asks how many fewer.

stem.en: Eva has 17 beads. Finn has 8 beads. How many fewer beads does Finn have than Eva?
stem.es: Eva tiene 17 cuentas. Finn tiene 8 cuentas. ¿Cuántas cuentas menos tiene Finn que Eva?

hints.en: Compare Finn's beads with Eva's beads.
How many more does Eva have than Finn?
Think: 8 plus what number makes 17?

objective: Solve a compare word problem that uses the word fewer.

stem.en: A bakery has 16 muffins. It has 9 fewer cookies than muffins. How many cookies does it have?
stem.es: Una panadería tiene 16 panecillos. Tiene 9 galletas menos que panecillos. ¿Cuántas galletas tiene?

choices.why: 9 is how many fewer, not how many cookies there are.
Fewer means less. Do not add.
That is one too few. Count back carefully.

hints.en: There are fewer cookies than muffins.
Start with the muffins and take away the 9 fewer.
Find 16 take away 9.

objective: Add tens and ones by hopping on a number line.

stem.en: Start at 50. Make two hops of 10, then three hops of 1. Mark where you land.
stem.es: Empieza en 50. Da dos saltos de 10 y luego tres saltos de 1. Marca dónde caes.

hints.en: Big hops of 10 land on a new ten.
After the big hops, make small hops of 1.
Count the small hops one at a time.

objective: Find the mistake in naming 4 equal shares.

stem.en: Sam cuts a circle into 4 equal parts and calls each part a half. Which step is the mistake?
stem.es: Sam corta un círculo en 4 partes iguales y llama a cada parte una mitad. ¿Qué paso es el error?

steps: The circle is cut into 4 equal parts.
Each part is one of 4 equal parts.
So each part is a half.

hints.en: A half is one of 2 equal parts.
How many equal parts does Sam's circle have?
The name depends on how many equal parts.

steps: 4 equal parts are called fourths, not halves.
solution.es: 4 partes iguales se llaman cuartos. Cada parte es un cuarto.

objective: Find the flaw in using a single attribute to name a shape.

stem.en: Jun says his shape is a square because it has 4 sides. Which step is the mistake?
stem.es: Jun dice que su figura es un cuadrado porque tiene 4 lados. ¿Qué paso es el error?

steps: So Jun's shape must be a square.

hints.en: A rectangle also has 4 sides.
Is 4 sides the only thing a square needs?
A square needs other attributes too.

steps: Other shapes, such as rectangles, also have 4 sides.
A square also needs all 4 sides the same length, so step 3 is the mistake.
solution.es: Otras figuras también tienen 4 lados. Un cuadrado necesita además lados iguales.

verify.note: Seeing that 4 sides alone does not define a square is conceptual reasoning about definitions, so a person should review the explanation.

objective: Know how many fourths make a whole.

stem.en: A square is cut into fourths. How many fourths put together make the whole square?
stem.es: Un cuadrado se corta en cuartos. ¿Cuántos cuartos juntos forman el cuadrado entero?

hints.en: The whole square is cut into equal parts.
Fourths means four equal parts.
Count all of the fourths.

steps: Fourths are 4 equal parts of the whole.
All 4 fourths make the whole square.
solution.es: Los 4 cuartos juntos forman el cuadrado entero.

objective: Subtract tens from 100 by hopping back on a number line.

stem.en: A frog sits at 100 on the line. It hops back by tens, 3 times. Mark where it lands.
stem.es: Una rana está en 100 en la recta. Salta hacia atrás de diez en diez, 3 veces. Marca dónde cae.

hints.en: Each hop back is ten less.
Hop to the left three times.
Say the number after each hop.

objective: Subtract within 10 in a take-from story.

stem.en: 5 frogs sit on a log. 2 frogs jump off. How many frogs are on the log now?
stem.es: 5 ranas están sobre un tronco. 2 ranas saltan al agua. ¿Cuántas ranas hay ahora en el tronco?

choices.why: Frogs left the log, so there are fewer. Subtract, do not add.
That is how many jumped off, not how many are left.
Count back again. 5 take away 2 is not 4.

hints.en: Frogs jumped off, so the number gets smaller.
Start with 5 and take 2 away.
Count back 2 from 5.

objective: Solve a subtraction problem by thinking of an unknown addend.

stem.en: Nia needs 15 points to win. She has 9. Think of 9 + ? = 15. How many more points does she need?
stem.es: Nia necesita 15 puntos para ganar. Tiene 9. Piensa en 9 + ? = 15. ¿Cuántos puntos más necesita?

hints.en: The question asks for the missing part.
Count up from 9 until you reach 15.
How many counts did you make?

objective: Find the step that leaves a gap when measuring with units.

stem.en: Mina measures a pencil that is really 6 cubes long. She says it is 5. Which step is the mistake?
stem.es: Mina mide un lápiz que en realidad mide 6 cubos. Ella dice que mide 5. ¿Qué paso es el error?

steps: Mina lays cubes along the pencil.
She leaves a gap between two cubes.
She counts 5 cubes and says the pencil is 5 cubes long.

hints.en: Cubes should touch each other.
Look at what happens between the cubes.
A gap uses up space that needs a cube.

steps: The gap hides space where a cube belongs.
With no gaps she would count 6 cubes.
solution.es: El espacio vacío oculta un cubo. Sin espacios habría contado 6 cubos.

objective: Find the unknown addend within 100.

stem.en: Ben has 43 stickers. After a gift he has 49. Solve 43 + n = 49 to find the gift.
stem.es: Ben tiene 43 calcomanías. Después de un regalo tiene 49. Resuelve 43 + n = 49 para hallar el regalo.

hints.en: Ben's tens did not change.
Only the ones digit grew, from 3 to 9.
How many ones do you add to 3 to get 9?

steps: 43 + n = 49 and the tens stay the same.
solution.es: Las unidades pasan de 3 a 9, así que n = 6.

objective: Find the starting amount in a take-away equation.

stem.en: Ella had n grapes. She ate 3 and has 4 left. Solve n − 3 = 4.
stem.es: Ella tenía n uvas. Se comió 3 y le quedan 4. Resuelve n − 3 = 4.

hints.en: n is how many grapes Ella had at first.
She ate 3 and kept 4.
Put the grapes she ate back with the ones she kept.

objective: Subtract within 10 in a take-from story.

stem.en: Rita has 9 grapes and eats 4. How many grapes does she have left?
stem.es: Rita tiene 9 uvas y se come 4. ¿Cuántas uvas le quedan?

choices.why: Eating grapes takes some away. Subtract, do not add.
That is how many she ate, not how many are left.
Count back carefully. 9 take away 4 is not 6.

hints.en: Rita eats some grapes, so fewer are left.
Start at 9 and count back.
Take 4 away from 9.

objective: Find the greatest of several two-digit numbers.

stem.en: Which is the greatest number: 64, 46, 60 or 6?
stem.es: ¿Cuál es el número mayor: 64, 46, 60 o 6?

choices.why: 46 has only 4 tens. Look for the most tens.
60 has the same tens as 64 but fewer ones.
6 is only 6 ones, the smallest number here.

hints.en: Find the number with the most tens first.
Two numbers have 6 tens. Compare their ones.
The greatest has 6 tens and the most ones.

steps: 64 has more ones than 60, so 64 is greatest.
solution.es: 64 y 60 tienen 6 decenas; 64 tiene más unidades, así que 64 es el mayor.

objective: Explain why regrouping addends does not change the total.

stem.en: Ben says (2 + 7) + 3 and 2 + (7 + 3) give different totals. Is he right? Explain.
stem.es: Ben dice que (2 + 7) + 3 y 2 + (7 + 3) dan totales distintos. ¿Tiene razón? Explica.

criteria.en: Says the totals are the same, 12
criteria.es: Dice que los totales son iguales, 12

criteria.en: Shows both ways, such as 7 + 3 making a ten
criteria.es: Muestra las dos formas, como 7 + 3 que forma una decena

sample.en: He is not right. (2 + 7) + 3 = 9 + 3 = 12 and 2 + (7 + 3) = 2 + 10 = 12. Grouping the numbers differently does not change the total.
sample.es: No tiene razón. (2 + 7) + 3 = 9 + 3 = 12 y 2 + (7 + 3) = 2 + 10 = 12. Agrupar distinto no cambia el total.

hints.en: The parentheses tell you which two numbers to add first.
Work out each side in two steps.
Compare the two totals you get.

objective: Critique a claim about the time one hour later.

stem.en: The clock shows 4:30. Ava says in 1 hour it will be 5:00. Is she right? Explain.
stem.es: El reloj marca las 4:30. Ava dice que dentro de 1 hora serán las 5:00. ¿Tiene razón? Explica.

criteria.en: Explains the hour goes up by 1 and the half hour stays
criteria.es: Explica que la hora sube 1 y la media hora se queda

sample.en: No. In 1 hour the hour number goes up by 1 but the 30 stays. It will be 5:30. 5:00 is only half an hour later.
sample.es: No. En 1 hora el número de la hora sube 1 pero los 30 se quedan. Serán las 5:30. Las 5:00 es solo media hora después.

hints.en: Start at 4:30 and think about one whole hour.
How long is it from 4:30 to 5:00?
One hour changes the hour number by 1.

steps: 5:00 is only a half hour after 4:30.
solution.es: Una hora después de las 4:30 son las 5:30; las 5:00 es solo media hora después.

objective: Find the mistake in reading the hour for half past.

stem.en: Bo reads a clock with the short hand between 5 and 6, and the long hand on 6. Which step is the mistake?
stem.es: Bo lee un reloj con la manecilla corta entre el 5 y el 6, y la larga en el 6. ¿Qué paso es el error?

steps: The short hand is between 5 and 6.
The long hand is on 6, so it is half past.
The short hand is near 6, so it is 6:30.

hints.en: At half past, the short hand is halfway between two numbers.
Has the short hand reached 6 yet?
Use the hour number the short hand passed.

steps: The short hand has passed 5 but has not reached 6.
solution.es: La corta pasó el 5 pero no llegó al 6: son las 5:30.

objective: Reason about how the size of a half depends on the whole.

stem.en: Is half of a small pizza the same size as half of a large pizza? Explain.
stem.es: ¿Es la mitad de una pizza pequeña del mismo tamaño que la mitad de una pizza grande? Explica.

criteria.en: Says no, the halves are different sizes
criteria.es: Dice que no, las mitades son de distinto tamaño

criteria.en: Says a half depends on the size of its whole
criteria.es: Dice que una mitad depende del tamaño de su entero

sample.en: No. A half is one of 2 equal parts of its own whole. A large pizza is bigger, so its half is bigger.
sample.es: No. Una mitad es una de 2 partes iguales de su propio entero. Una pizza grande es más grande, así que su mitad es más grande.

hints.en: Picture a small pizza and a large pizza.
Cut each into 2 equal parts.
Compare one part from each pizza.

steps: Each pizza is cut into 2 equal parts.
The large pizza's half is bigger because its whole is bigger.
solution.es: La pizza grande es más grande, así que su mitad también es más grande.

verify.note: Reasoning that a half depends on the size of its whole is a conceptual explanation with no computation, so a person should review it.

objective: Explain why the parts of a half must be equal.

stem.en: Two friends share a cracker. Why must the two pieces be equal to be called halves?
stem.es: Dos amigos comparten una galleta. ¿Por qué las dos piezas deben ser iguales para llamarse mitades?

criteria.en: Says halves are 2 equal shares of the whole
criteria.es: Dice que las mitades son 2 partes iguales del entero

criteria.en: Says if one piece is bigger, the sharing is not fair or they are not halves
criteria.es: Dice que si una pieza es más grande, el reparto no es justo o no son mitades

sample.en: A half is one of 2 equal parts. If one piece is bigger, the pieces are not the same size, so they are not halves.
sample.es: Una mitad es una de 2 partes iguales. Si una pieza es más grande, no tienen el mismo tamaño, así que no son mitades.

hints.en: Think about sharing fairly with a friend.
What would happen if one piece were bigger?
A half means the same amount as the other half.

solution.es: Las mitades son 2 partes iguales; si no son iguales, no son mitades.

verify.note: Explaining why halves must be equal is conceptual reasoning in words, so a person should review the explanation.

objective: Compare two group sizes and name the bigger number.

stem.en: A farm has 65 hens and 56 ducks. Which group is bigger? Write the number in the bigger group.
stem.es: Una granja tiene 65 gallinas y 56 patos. ¿Qué grupo es más grande? Escribe el número del grupo más grande.

criteria.en: Compares the tens first: 6 tens and 5 tens
criteria.es: Compara primero las decenas: 6 decenas y 5 decenas

sample.en: 65 has 6 tens and 56 has 5 tens, so 65 is greater. The hens are the bigger group.
sample.es: 65 tiene 6 decenas y 56 tiene 5, así que 65 es mayor. Las gallinas son el grupo más grande.

hints.en: Compare the two numbers by their tens.
Which number has more tens?
The bigger number is the bigger group.

solution.es: 65 > 56, así que el grupo más grande son las gallinas.

objective: Find the hour two hours later.

stem.en: It is 8:00 now. What hour will it be in 2 hours? Write the hour number.
stem.es: Ahora son las 8:00. ¿Qué hora será dentro de 2 horas? Escribe el número de la hora.

hints.en: Later means the hour number goes up.
Count on 2 hours from 8.
8 and 2 more.

steps: 2 hours later adds 2 to the hour.

objective: Jump back by tens on a number line.

stem.en: Start at 70. Jump back 10, two times. Mark where you land.
stem.es: Empieza en 70. Salta hacia atrás 10, dos veces. Marca dónde caes.

hints.en: Each jump back is 10 less.
The number line is marked every 10.
Make two jumps to the left.

objective: Name the number just before 100.

stem.en: Which number comes just before 100?
stem.es: ¿Qué número viene justo antes del 100?

choices.why: 101 comes after 100, not before.
90 is ten before 100. Just before means one before.
10 is far from 100.

hints.en: Before means counting backward.
Count back one from 100.
What number is said right before 100 when you count?

objective: Find the least of several two-digit numbers.

stem.en: Ming has cards numbered 72, 27, 70 and 17. Which card shows the least number?
stem.es: Ming tiene tarjetas con los números 72, 27, 70 y 17. ¿Qué tarjeta muestra el número menor?

choices.why: 72 has 7 tens. Look for fewer tens.
27 is small, but another card has fewer tens.
70 has 7 tens, more than 17.

hints.en: The least number has the fewest tens.
Only one card has just 1 ten.
Compare the tens of all four cards.

steps: 17 has 1 ten, 27 has 2 tens, 70 and 72 have 7 tens.
solution.es: 17 tiene solo 1 decena, así que es el menor.

objective: Match length descriptions to total lengths in whole units.

stem.en: Match each length description to the total length.
stem.es: Relaciona cada descripción con la longitud total.

hints.en: Work out each description.
Keep the unit the same: cubes or clips.
Subtract for the part that is cut off.

objective: Explain what the long hand on 6 means.

stem.en: Maya says, 'The long hand on 6 means 6 o'clock.' Is she right? Explain.
stem.es: Maya dice: «La manecilla larga en el 6 significa las 6 en punto». ¿Tiene razón? Explica.

criteria.en: Says no, the long hand on 6 means half past
criteria.es: Dice que no, la larga en 6 significa y media

criteria.en: Says the short hand tells the hour, or that 6 × 5 = 30 minutes
criteria.es: Dice que la corta indica la hora, o que 6 × 5 = 30 minutos

sample.en: No. The long hand on 6 means 30 minutes after the hour, or half past. The short hand tells the hour. Each number on the clock is 5 minutes, and 6 × 5 = 30.
sample.es: No. La manecilla larga en el 6 significa 30 minutos después de la hora, o y media. La corta indica la hora. Cada número del reloj son 5 minutos, y 6 × 5 = 30.

hints.en: Which hand tells the hour?
Count by 5s to the 6 on the clock face.
What does the long hand on 12 mean? Compare it with 6.

steps: Counting by 5s to the 6 gives 30 minutes.
So the long hand on 6 means half past, not 6 o'clock.
solution.es: Contando de 5 en 5 hasta el 6 se llega a 30 minutos: es y media.

objective: Sort objects as longer or shorter than a reference length.

stem.en: The pencil is 6 cubes long. Sort each object: is it longer or shorter than the pencil?
stem.es: El lápiz mide 6 cubos. Clasifica cada objeto: ¿es más largo o más corto que el lápiz?

hints.en: Compare each length with 6 cubes.
A bigger number of cubes means a longer object.
6 cubes is the pencil. 5 cubes is just under it.

solution.es: 9, 8 y 7 cubos son más de 6; 3, 5 y 1 cubos son menos de 6.

objective: Add by making the next ten first.

stem.es: Lena usa 2 de los 4 para convertir 38 en 40. Luego suma lo que queda. ¿Cuánto es 38 + 4?

choices.why: That adds all 4 to 40. Lena already used 2 of the 4.
Lena is not finished. She still has to add the rest of the 4.

hints.en: Lena splits the 4 into 2 and another part.
How much of the 4 is left after the first 2?
Add the leftover part to 40.

objective: Add by making a ten first.

stem.es: Ira resuelve 8 + 5 formando una decena: 8 + 2 = 10. Luego suma 3 más. ¿Cuál es el total?

hints.en: Ira split the 5 into 2 and 3.
She made a ten with the 8 and the 2.
Now add the leftover 3 to the ten.

objective: Choose the two addends that make ten when adding three numbers.

stem.en: To add 6 + 4 + 8, Rosa wants to make a ten first. Which two numbers should she add first?

choices.why: 6 + 8 makes 14, not a ten.
4 + 8 makes 12, not a ten.

hints.en: A ten is the number 10.
Look for two numbers that fit together to make 10.
Which pair of 6, 4 and 8 adds to 10?

objective: Add three numbers by making a ten with two of them.

stem.en: Ava adds 3 + 9 + 1 by making a ten with 9 and 1. What is the total?
stem.es: Ava suma 3 + 9 + 1 formando una decena con 9 y 1. ¿Cuál es el total?

choices.why: 10 is only the 9 and the 1. Do not forget the 3.
Check again: 10 and 3 more is more than 12.
That is one too many. 10 + 3 is not 14.

hints.en: Add 9 and 1 first to make a ten.
Now you have 10 and the 3 still to add.
Count on 3 from 10.

objective: Find the mistake when a number is moved to make a ten.

stem.en: Ana makes a ten to solve 9 + 6. Which step has the mistake?
stem.es: Ana forma una decena para resolver 9 + 6. ¿Qué paso tiene el error?

steps: Take 1 from the 6 and give it to the 9.

hints.en: Ana moves 1 from one number to the other.
Look at what the 6 turned into.
If the 6 gave away 1, what is left?

steps: The 6 gave 1 away, so it is now 5.

objective: Choose the addition question that matches a subtraction story.

stem.en: Kofi has 13 marbles. He gives 6 to his sister. Which addition question helps him find how many are left?
stem.es: Kofi tiene 13 canicas. Le da 6 a su hermana. ¿Qué pregunta de suma le ayuda a hallar cuántas quedan?

choices.why: This adds the marbles together. Kofi gave marbles away.
This also adds. The story takes marbles away.
13 plus any number cannot make 6, a smaller number.

hints.en: Kofi started with 13 and gave some away.
Think: the marbles left and 6 given make what number?
6 plus the marbles left makes the 13 he started with.

steps: The 6 marbles given and the marbles left make 13.
solution.es: Las 6 canicas que da y las que quedan forman 13: 6 + ? = 13.

hints.en: Gus got one more ten.
Take that ten away to go back to the start.
62 has 6 tens. Take away 1 ten.

sample.en: 3 boxes of 10 is 30. 30 + 8 = 38 markers.
sample.es: 3 cajas de 10 son 30. 30 + 8 = 38 marcadores.

hints.en: Each box holds a ten.
Count the boxes by tens.
Add the single markers last.

stem.es: Relaciona cada suma con su resultado.

9 + 9 is a double.

stem.en: Draw a line from each addition problem to the total it makes.
stem.es: Une cada problema de suma con el total que forma.

hints.en: Add the tens when you add a multiple of ten.

27 + 3 makes a new ten.

objective: Order three lengths and find the middle one.

stem.en: Three crayons measure 8 cubes, 3 cubes and 5 cubes. Which length is in the middle when you order them?
stem.es: Tres crayones miden 8 cubos, 3 cubos y 5 cubos. ¿Cuál longitud queda en el medio al ordenarlos?

choices.why: 8 cubes is the longest crayon, not the middle one.
3 cubes is the shortest crayon, not the middle one.
That adds all three lengths. The question asks which one is in the middle.

hints.en: Put the lengths in order from shortest to longest.
Find the shortest and the longest first.
The middle length is the one left over.

solution.es: En orden: 3, 5, 8. La del medio es 5 cubos.

objective: Use side counts to find an unknown shape's number of sides.

stem.en: Max draws a triangle, a rectangle and a mystery shape. Together they have 12 sides. How many sides does the mystery shape have?
stem.es: Max dibuja un triángulo, un rectángulo y una figura misteriosa. Juntas tienen 12 lados. ¿Cuántos lados tiene la figura misteriosa?

criteria.en: Uses 3 sides for the triangle and 4 for the rectangle
criteria.es: Usa 3 lados para el triángulo y 4 para el rectángulo

criteria.en: Finds the mystery shape has 5 sides
criteria.es: Halla que la figura misteriosa tiene 5 lados

sample.en: 3 + 4 = 7 sides. 12 − 7 = 5, so the mystery shape has 5 sides.
sample.es: 3 + 4 = 7 lados. 12 − 7 = 5, así que la figura misteriosa tiene 5 lados.

hints.en: A triangle has 3 sides and a rectangle has 4 sides.
Add the sides you know.
Take that number away from 11.

objective: Use a known double to find a near double.

hints.en: 6 is one more than 5.

Add one to ten.

stem.en: Zoe solves 90 − 40. Which step has the mistake?
stem.es: Zoe resuelve 90 − 40. ¿Qué paso tiene el error?

hints.en: Tens are worth ten each.

Write 5 tens as a number with a zero.

objective: Explain why length units must not overlap or leave gaps.

stem.en: Why should there be no gaps and no overlaps when you measure with cubes?
stem.es: ¿Por qué no debe haber espacios ni cubos encimados cuando mides con cubos?

criteria.en: Says gaps make you count too few cubes
criteria.es: Dice que los espacios hacen contar menos cubos

criteria.en: Says overlaps make you count too many cubes
criteria.es: Dice que los cubos encimados hacen contar más cubos

sample.en: If there is a gap, you count too few cubes. If cubes overlap, you count too many. The cubes must touch end to end to show the true length.
sample.es: Si hay un espacio, cuentas menos cubos. Si los cubos están encimados, cuentas más. Los cubos deben tocarse extremo con extremo para mostrar la longitud real.

hints.en: Picture a pencil covered by cubes with a gap.
What would you count if two cubes sat on top of each other?
The count should match the true length.

steps: A gap leaves out space, so the count is too small.
An overlap counts space twice, so the count is too big.
solution.es: Un espacio da un conteo menor y un cubo encimado da un conteo mayor.

verify.note: Explaining why measurement units must be placed without gaps or overlaps is reasoning in words, so a person should review the explanation.

objective: Use a number bond to see the parts of ten.

stem.en: Make a number bond with 10 as the whole. Set the left part to 4 so the bond shows both parts.
stem.es: Haz un enlace numérico con 10 como el total. Pon 4 en la parte izquierda para que se vean las dos partes.

hints.en: The whole is 10. The parts add up to the whole.
Set one part to 4. The other part changes by itself.
Watch the right circle after you set the left part.

solution.es: 4 + 6 = 10, así que la otra parte es 6.

objective: Use a number bond to find a missing part.

hints.en: The whole is 12. The two parts add up to the whole.

Read the other part that appears.

solution.es: La otra parte es 7, así que 12 − 5 = 7.

The pond started with 9 ducks, not 4.
13 is the answer, not a starting number. Start with 9 and 4.

Joining means the total gets bigger.

objective: Name one part of a shape cut into 4 equal parts.

stem.en: Leo lines up a pencil and a marker on a ruler. He says the marker is longer. Which step is the mistake?
stem.es: Leo alinea un lápiz y un marcador en una regla. Dice que el marcador es más largo. ¿Qué paso es el error?

steps: The pencil goes from the 0 mark to the 7 mark.
The marker goes from the 2 mark to the 8 mark.
The marker ends at 8, so it is longer.

hints.en: Objects should start at the same place to compare ends.
Where does the marker start?
Work out how long each object really is.

steps: The marker starts at 2, so its length is 8 − 2 = 6.
The pencil is 7 long, so the pencil is longer.
solution.es: El marcador empieza en 2, así que mide 8 − 2 = 6. El lápiz mide 7 y es más largo.

objective: Find the flaw in claiming two different subtractions are equal.

stem.en: Ravi says 9 − 4 and 9 − 5 have the same answer because both start with 9. Which step is wrong?
stem.es: Ravi dice que 9 − 4 y 9 − 5 tienen la misma respuesta porque las dos empiezan con 9. ¿Qué paso está mal?

steps: So the answers must be the same.

hints.en: Work out both subtractions.
The starting number is the same. What is different?
Taking away more leaves less.

steps: A different number is taken away, so the answers are different.
solution.es: 9 − 4 = 5 y 9 − 5 = 4: se quita un número distinto, así que las respuestas son distintas.

objective: Find an expression with the same total after changing the order of three addends.

stem.en: Which expression has the same total as 3 + 4 + 6?
stem.es: ¿Qué expresión tiene el mismo total que 3 + 4 + 6?

choices.why: 3 + 4 + 5 is one less, because 5 is not 6.
3 + 6 + 6 uses 6 twice. The 4 is missing.
3 + 4 + 4 uses 4 twice. The 6 is missing.

hints.en: The same three numbers can be added in any order.
Look for the choice that has 3, 4 and 6.
Check that no number is changed.

solution.es: 4 + 6 + 3 usa 3, 4 y 6, y da 13 igual que 3 + 4 + 6.

objective: Match expressions that have the same value.

stem.en: Match each addition to another addition that has the same value.
stem.es: Relaciona cada suma con otra suma que tenga el mismo valor.

hints.en: Work out the total of each addition.
Two additions match when their totals are equal.
Check each pair with the equal sign.

objective: Count halves when several shapes are cut in half.

stem.en: Lia cuts 3 sandwiches in half. How many halves does she have in all?
stem.es: Lia corta 3 sándwiches por la mitad. ¿Cuántas mitades tiene en total?

criteria.es: Ve que cada sándwich da 2 mitades

sample.en: Each sandwich makes 2 halves. 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 halves.
sample.es: Cada sándwich da 2 mitades. 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 mitades.

hints.en: Each sandwich is cut into the same number of halves.
How many halves does one sandwich make?
Add that number three times.

objective: Find an unknown addend in a story equation.

stem.en: A pot has 5 seeds. Mia adds n more seeds. Now there are 9. Solve 5 + n = 9.
stem.es: Una maceta tiene 5 semillas. Mia agrega n semillas más. Ahora hay 9. Resuelve 5 + n = 9.

hints.en: n is the number of seeds Mia added.
Count up from 5 to 9.
How many counts did it take?

objective: Identify shapes with four straight sides.

stem.en: Select ALL the shapes that have 4 straight sides.
stem.es: Selecciona TODAS las figuras que tienen 4 lados rectos.

choices.why: A triangle has 3 sides.
A circle has no straight sides.

hints.en: Count the straight sides of each shape.
The shapes with 4 sides are called four-sided shapes.
Three of the five shapes have 4 sides.

steps: Square, rectangle and trapezoid have 4 sides.
Triangle has 3 sides and circle has none.
solution.es: Cuadrado, rectángulo y trapecio tienen 4 lados.

objective: Identify which clock times are half past.

stem.en: Select ALL the times that are half past an hour.
stem.es: Selecciona TODAS las horas que son y media.

choices.why: 6:00 is on the hour, not half past.
12:00 is on the hour, not half past.

hints.en: Half past means 30 minutes after the hour.
Look at the numbers after the colon.
Three times end in 30.

solution.es: 3:30, 9:30 y 11:30 son y media; 6:00 y 12:00 son en punto.

objective: Identify which descriptions show halves.

stem.en: Select ALL the shapes that are cut into halves.
stem.es: Selecciona TODAS las figuras que están cortadas en mitades.

text.en: A square cut into 2 equal parts
text.es: Un cuadrado cortado en 2 partes iguales

text.en: A circle cut into 4 equal parts
text.es: Un círculo cortado en 4 partes iguales

choices.why: 4 equal parts are fourths, not halves.

text.en: A rectangle cut into 2 equal parts
text.es: Un rectángulo cortado en 2 partes iguales

text.en: A circle cut into 2 parts, one much bigger
text.es: Un círculo cortado en 2 partes, una mucho más grande

choices.why: Halves must be equal. One part is bigger here.

text.en: A rectangle cut into 3 equal parts
text.es: Un rectángulo cortado en 3 partes iguales

choices.why: 3 equal parts are thirds, not halves.

hints.en: Halves are 2 equal parts.
Count the parts, and check they are equal.
Two of the five shapes show halves.

steps: The square and the first rectangle are each cut into 2 equal parts.
The others have 4 parts, unequal parts, or 3 parts.
solution.es: El cuadrado y el primer rectángulo están cortados en 2 partes iguales.

objective: Explain how an addition fact helps with a related subtraction.

stem.en: Explain how 7 + 5 = 12 can help you solve 12 − 7.
stem.es: Explica cómo 7 + 5 = 12 te puede ayudar a resolver 12 − 7.

criteria.en: Says 12 is the total and 7 is one part
criteria.es: Dice que 12 es el total y 7 es una parte

criteria.en: Says the other part, 5, is the answer to 12 − 7
criteria.es: Dice que la otra parte, 5, es la respuesta de 12 − 7

sample.en: 7 + 5 = 12, so 12 take away 7 leaves the other part, 5. 12 − 7 = 5.
sample.es: 7 + 5 = 12, así que a 12 al quitarle 7 le queda la otra parte, 5. 12 − 7 = 5.

hints.en: Think of 12 as the whole and 7 as one part.
What is the other part?
The parts of a whole add up to the whole.

steps: The whole is 12 and one part is 7.
solution.es: El total es 12 y una parte es 7; la otra parte es 5, entonces 12 − 7 = 5.

objective: Explain how a basic fact helps subtract multiples of ten.

stem.en: Use the fact 7 − 4 to explain, in your own words, how to subtract 70 − 40.
stem.es: Usa el hecho 7 − 4 para explicar con tus palabras cómo restar 70 − 40.

criteria.en: Says 70 is 7 tens and 40 is 4 tens
criteria.es: Dice que 70 es 7 decenas y 40 es 4 decenas

sample.en: 70 is 7 tens and 40 is 4 tens. 7 − 4 = 3, so 3 tens is 30. So 70 − 40 = 30.
sample.es: 70 es 7 decenas y 40 es 4 decenas. 7 − 4 = 3, así que 3 decenas es 30. Entonces 70 − 40 = 30.

hints.en: Say 70 and 40 as numbers of tens.
Subtract the tens using a basic fact.
The answer is also a number of tens.

objective: Subtract tens from tens within 100.

stem.en: What is 70 − 20?
stem.es: ¿Cuánto es 70 − 20?

choices.why: That adds. We are taking away 20.
7 − 2 = 5 tens, which is 50, not 5 ones.
That takes away only 10. Twenty is 2 tens.

hints.en: Think of 70 as 7 tens and 20 as 2 tens.
Subtract the tens.
Write the answer as tens: how many tens, then a zero.

objective: Identify the shape with no straight sides.

stem.en: Which shape has no straight sides?
stem.es: ¿Qué figura no tiene lados rectos?

choices.why: A triangle has 3 straight sides.
A square has 4 straight sides.
A rectangle has 4 straight sides.

hints.en: Think about the sides of each shape.
Which shape is round?
Pick the shape with no corners.

steps: Triangle, square and rectangle all have straight sides.
solution.es: El círculo no tiene lados rectos.

objective: Solve a subtraction equation with the start unknown.

stem.en: Dara had n shells. She gave away 4 and has 9 left. Solve n − 4 = 9.
stem.es: Dara tenía n conchas. Regaló 4 y le quedan 9. Resuelve n − 4 = 9.

hints.en: n is the number of shells Dara had at the start.
She gave 4 away and kept 9.
Put the 4 shells back with the 9.

objective: Find how much longer one object is using the same unit.

stem.en: A shoe is 6 paper clips long. A book is 9 paper clips long. How many more paper clips long is the book?
stem.es: Un zapato mide 6 clips de largo. Un libro mide 9 clips de largo. ¿Cuántos clips más largo es el libro?

choices.why: That adds the two lengths. The question asks how many more.
Count from 6 up to 9 again. That is one too many.
9 is the length of the book, not the difference.

hints.en: Compare the two lengths.
The book is longer. How much longer?
Count up from 6 to 9.

solution.es: 9 − 6 = 3. El libro es 3 clips más largo.

objective: Use side counts of two shapes together.

stem.en: A square has 4 sides. A triangle has 3 sides. How many sides do the two shapes have together?
stem.es: Un cuadrado tiene 4 lados. Un triángulo tiene 3 lados. ¿Cuántos lados tienen las dos figuras juntas?

hints.en: Put the sides of both shapes together.
Start at 4 and count on.
Count on 3 from 4.

objective: Rewrite a subtraction as an addition with an unknown and solve.

stem.en: To find 14 − 6, solve 6 + n = 14. What is n?
stem.es: Para hallar 14 − 6, resuelve 6 + n = 14. ¿Cuánto vale n?

hints.en: n is the missing part of 14.
Count up from 6 to 14.
Go to 10 first, then to 14.

objective: Compose larger shapes from smaller ones and count the small pieces.

stem.en: 4 small squares make 1 big square. Lin makes 3 big squares. How many small squares does she use?
stem.es: 4 cuadrados pequeños forman 1 cuadrado grande. Lin hace 3 cuadrados grandes. ¿Cuántos cuadrados pequeños usa?

sample.en: 3 big squares need 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 small squares.
sample.es: 3 cuadrados grandes necesitan 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 cuadrados pequeños.

hints.en: Each big square uses the same number of small squares.
Make 3 groups of 4.
Add 4 three times.

steps: Each big square uses 4 small squares.

objective: Read a data set to find the category with the most.

stem.en: Votes for a snack: apples 6, popcorn 9, grapes 3. Which snack got the most votes?
stem.es: Votos para una merienda: manzanas 6, palomitas 9, uvas 3. ¿Qué merienda recibió más votos?

choices.why: Apples got 6 votes. Another snack got more.
Grapes got only 3 votes, the fewest.

hints.en: Look for the biggest number of votes.
Compare 6, 9 and 3.
The snack with the biggest number wins.

steps: 9 is the greatest, so popcorn got the most.
solution.es: 9 es el número mayor: las palomitas recibieron más votos.

objective: Sort numbers by comparing them with 50.

stem.en: Sort each number: is it greater than 50 or less than 50?
stem.es: Clasifica cada número: ¿es mayor que 50 o menor que 50?

hints.en: Compare the tens digit with the 5 in 50.
More than 5 tens means greater than 50.
Careful: 55 has 5 tens like 50, so look at its ones too.

solution.es: 61, 74 y 55 son mayores que 50; 38, 47 y 29 son menores.

objective: Sort two-digit numbers by how many tens they have.

stem.en: Sort each number by how many tens it has.
stem.es: Clasifica cada número según cuántas decenas tiene.

hints.en: Look at the first digit of each number.
The first digit tells how many tens.
Put numbers with the same first digit together.

objective: Sort digital times into on the hour and half past.

stem.en: Sort each time: is it on the hour or half past?
stem.es: Clasifica cada hora: ¿es en punto o y media?

hints.en: Look at the numbers after the colon.
00 means exactly on the hour.
30 means half an hour past.

solution.es: Los que terminan en 00 son en punto; los que terminan en 30 son y media.

objective: Sort shapes by a defining attribute, the number of sides.

stem.en: Sort the shapes by how many straight sides they have.
stem.es: Clasifica las figuras según cuántos lados rectos tienen.

hints.en: Count the sides of each shape.
Size does not change the number of sides.
A triangle is the shape with 3 sides.

steps: Both triangles have 3 sides, big or small.
Square, rectangle and rhombus each have 4 sides.
solution.es: Los dos triángulos tienen 3 lados; cuadrado, rectángulo y rombo tienen 4.

verify.note: Classifying named shapes by number of sides depends on shape definitions and pictures; no computation proves it, so a person should review the shape list.

objective: Sort categories by whether their count is more than a benchmark.

stem.en: Sort each lunch by its votes: more than 5 votes, or 5 votes or fewer.
stem.es: Clasifica cada almuerzo por sus votos: más de 5 votos, o 5 votos o menos.

hints.en: Look at the number of votes for each lunch.
Compare each number with 5.
Exactly 5 votes belongs with the fewer group.

solution.es: 8, 6 y 7 son más de 5; 3, 2 y 5 son 5 o menos.

objective: Subtract ten from a two-digit number in a context.

stem.en: Hana is on step 72 of a long staircase. She goes down 10 steps. Which step is she on now?
stem.es: Hana está en el escalón 72 de una escalera larga. Baja 10 escalones. ¿En qué escalón está ahora?

hints.en: Going down 10 steps is 10 less.
Change the tens digit only.
7 tens becomes how many tens?

solution.es: 10 menos: 7 decenas pasan a 6, o sea 62.

objective: Use 10 more to solve a game-points story.

sample.en: 67 has 6 tens. One more ten makes 7 tens. So Luis has 77 points.
sample.es: 67 tiene 6 decenas. Una decena más son 7 decenas. Luis tiene 77 puntos.

hints.en: A star gives exactly one more ten.
Only the tens digit changes.
6 tens and one more ten make how many tens?

objective: Find an unknown addend by subtracting.

hints.en: Nina started with 16 and some were given away.
The stickers she kept and the stickers she gave make 16.
Think: 7 plus what number makes 16?

objective: Choose the equation that matches a story with an unknown start.

stem.en: Maya had some stickers. She got 5 more and now has 12. Which equation can find how many she had?
stem.es: Maya tenía algunas calcomanías. Recibió 5 más y ahora tiene 12. ¿Qué ecuación sirve para hallar cuántas tenía?

choices.why: This adds the 5 to the total again. Maya already has 12 now.
You cannot take a bigger number from 5 to get 12.
This means she gave 5 away. In the story she got 5 more.

hints.en: n stands for the stickers Maya had at first.
She got more stickers, so the number grew.
The start plus 5 makes 12.

solution.es: Lo que tenía más 5 es 12: n + 5 = 12.

verify.note: Choosing an equation that matches a story is about the structure of the situation; the distractors are reasoned, not computed, so a person should review them.

objective: Sort subtraction of tens by the size of the difference.

stem.en: Work out each answer. Is it less than 40 or more than 40?
stem.es: Halla cada resultado. ¿Es menor que 40 o mayor que 40?

hints.en: Find each difference using tens.
Compare each answer with 40.
Four tens is 40.

solution.es: 20, 30 y 10 son menores que 40; 50, 70 y 50 son mayores que 40.

Add the jump to 10 and the jump from 10 to 16.

objective: Sort addition facts by comparing the sum with ten.

stem.es: Clasifica cada suma por su resultado: 10 o menos, o más de 10.

hints.en: Find each sum first.
Is the sum bigger than ten?
Ten itself goes in the first group.

solution.es: Las sumas 9, 10 y 9 son 10 o menos; 12, 13 y 16 son más de 10.

stem.es: Completa el cuadro para que la oración sea verdadera: 6 + 9 = 9 + □

hints.en: The same two numbers are on both sides.
On the right side, the 9 comes first.
Which number is added to the 9?

solution.es: Los dos lados usan 6 y 9, entonces el cuadro es 6.

stem.es: Una pecera tiene 11 peces. 4 peces son dorados y el resto son plateados. ¿Cuántos peces son plateados?

hints.en: The gold fish are one part of the 11. The silver fish are the other part.
Take the gold fish away from the whole group.

steps: The whole is 11 and one part is 4.

objective: Subtract tens with base-ten blocks.

stem.es: Empieza con 6 barras de decenas. Quita 2 barras de decenas.

Take away rods, one at a time.
Remove a tens rod two times.

steps: He ate 5 apples, so some are gone.

hints.en: Ben ate some apples, so fewer apples are left.
Look for the step that does not match the story.
Check whether the number sentence should add or subtract.

steps: Ben ate apples, so the number goes down.

stem.es: Había 15 pájaros en una cerca. 7 se fueron volando. ¿Cuántos pájaros hay ahora en la cerca?

choices.why: That is how many flew away, not how many are left.
Birds flew away, so the group gets smaller. Subtract, do not add.
Check by adding: 9 and 7 do not make 15.

hints.en: Some birds leave, so the group gets smaller.
Start with all the birds and take away the ones that flew.
Count back 7 from 15, or think 7 + ? = 15.

hints.en: Check each addition step.
The first sum, 5 + 3, is correct.
Count on 4 from 8 carefully.

objective: Match tally marks to the number they show.

stem.en: Match each tally to the number it shows. A group of five is shown as |||||.
stem.es: Relaciona cada conteo con marcas con el número que muestra. Un grupo de cinco se muestra como |||||.

Each group of five is |||||.
Add the groups of five to the leftover marks.

objective: Fill a ten-frame to see how many more make ten.

stem.es: El cuadro de diez muestra 7 fichas. Agrega fichas hasta llenarlo.

hints.en: A full ten-frame has 10 counters.
Look at how many empty spaces are left.
Press add once for each empty space.

stem.es: ¿Cuánto es 10 menos que 58?

stem.es: ¿Qué número es 10 menos que 100?

objective: Find the step that adds 1 instead of 10.

solution.es: 10 más significa sumar 1 a las decenas: 47 pasa a 57.

stem.en: Match each phrase to the number it names.

hints.en: More means the tens digit goes up by 1.

The ones digit stays the same.

stem.es: Rey dice que 40 + 30 es como sumar 4 decenas y 3 decenas. Explica por qué eso funciona.

criteria.en: Says 4 tens and 3 tens make 7 tens
criteria.es: Dice que 4 decenas y 3 decenas forman 7 decenas

sample.en: 40 is 4 tens and 30 is 3 tens. 4 tens + 3 tens = 7 tens, and 7 tens is 70.
sample.es: 40 es 4 decenas y 30 es 3 decenas. 4 decenas + 3 decenas = 7 decenas, y 7 decenas es 70.

hints.en: Say 40 and 30 as numbers of tens.
Add 4 and 3, then think about what a ten is worth.
Each ten is worth ten.

stem.en: Which is greater: 3 tens and 8 ones, or 4 tens and 2 ones? Explain how you know.

criteria.es: Dice que 4 decenas y 2 unidades es mayor

criteria.es: Compara primero las decenas, aunque 8 unidades es más que 2 unidades

hints.en: Write each one as a two-digit number.
Which place has more value, tens or ones?
Compare the tens first.

steps: 42 > 38 because 4 tens is more than 3 tens.
solution.es: 38 y 42: 42 es mayor porque 4 decenas es más que 3 decenas.

objective: Find the step that adds a one-digit number to the tens place.

stem.es: Pia suma 43 + 5. ¿Qué paso tiene el error?

steps: Add the 5 to the tens: 9 tens.

stem.es: ¿Cuántas decenas hay en el número 58?

hints.en: Tens are the bundles of ten.

stem.es: El número 42 está formado por cuántas decenas y cuántas unidades?

choices.why: That is 24. The first digit of 42 is the tens digit.
That adds the digits. The 4 and the 2 stand for tens and ones.
42 is the whole number, not the number of tens.

The last digit is in the ones place.
Read the digits one at a time.

objective: Subtract multiples of ten in a story problem.

stem.en: A theater has 90 seats. 60 seats have people in them. How many seats are empty?
stem.es: Un teatro tiene 90 asientos. 60 asientos están ocupados. ¿Cuántos asientos están vacíos?

sample.en: 9 tens − 6 tens = 3 tens. So 90 − 60 = 30 empty seats.
sample.es: 9 decenas − 6 decenas = 3 decenas. Entonces 90 − 60 = 30 asientos vacíos.

hints.en: Empty seats are the seats left after the full ones.
Use tens: 9 tens and 6 tens.
Subtract the tens, then say the number.

steps: Empty seats = all seats − full seats.

objective: Find the start number in a subtraction story.

stem.en: Think of a number. Take away 6 and 5 is left. What was the number?

hints.en: Work backward from the 5 that is left.
Undo taking away by putting the 6 back.
Add 6 to the number that is left.

objective: Find the addition mistake in a three-addend sum.

stem.en: Jo adds three numbers, 5 + 5 + 6, and shows her work. Which step is not correct?
stem.es: Jo suma tres números, 5 + 5 + 6, y muestra su trabajo. ¿Qué paso no es correcto?

hints.en: Check each step one at a time.
Step 1 is correct. Look at step 2.
Count on 6 from 10 carefully.

solution.es: 10 + 6 = 16, no 15. El paso 2 tiene el error.

objective: Find the unknown addend in a sum of three numbers.

stem.es: Una bolsa tiene 4 manzanas, n peras y 3 ciruelas. Hay 12 frutas. Resuelve 4 + n + 3 = 12.

hints.en: First add the numbers you know: 4 and 3.
The known fruit and the pears make 12 together.
What number added to 7 makes 12?

objective: Identify three-addend sums that equal a target total.

stem.en: Which of these sums of three numbers are equal to 12? Choose every correct one.

choices.why: 7 + 2 + 2 makes 11. It is one short of 12.
4 + 4 + 3 makes 11, not 12.

hints.en: Work out each sum one at a time.
Look for two numbers that make a ten first.
Three sums make 12 and two do not.

solution.es: 5+4+3, 6+3+3 y 2+8+2 dan 12; las otras dos dan 11.

objective: Solve a word problem that adds three numbers within 20.

hints.en: There are three kinds of birds. Add all of them.
Look for two groups that make a ten.
Add 6 and 4 first, then the swans.

objective: Solve a word problem that adds three whole numbers.

hints.en: Find the total of all three colors.
Add two groups first, then add the third.

Check that your three numbers are all different.

objective: Name a shape from the number of its straight sides.

A circle has no straight sides.
A hexagon has 6 sides.

steps: Count the sides of each shape.

objective: Subtract within 20 in a spending story.

sample.en: 18 − 9 = 9, because 9 + 9 = 18. Omar has 9 tickets left.
sample.es: 18 − 9 = 9, porque 9 + 9 = 18. A Omar le quedan 9 boletos.

hints.en: Spending tickets means fewer tickets are left.
Is there a double fact that can help?
Think: what number plus 9 makes 18?

steps: He spends some tickets, so subtract.

objective: Add two small numbers in a story.

objective: Treat ten ones as a bundle of one ten.

hints.en: Ten ones cubes can be bundled into one tens rod.
The number stays the same when you trade.
Use the trade button once.

solution.es: 10 unidades son 1 decena: 3 decenas y 3 unidades.

objective: Describe how two shapes are alike and different using attributes.

stem.en: How are a triangle and a rectangle alike? How are they different?
stem.es: ¿En qué se parecen un triángulo y un rectángulo? ¿En qué son diferentes?

criteria.en: Names a way they are alike, such as both have straight sides and corners
criteria.es: Dice en qué se parecen, como que ambos tienen lados rectos y esquinas

criteria.en: Names a difference, such as 3 sides and 3 corners versus 4 sides and 4 corners
criteria.es: Dice una diferencia, como 3 lados y 3 esquinas frente a 4 lados y 4 esquinas

sample.en: Both have straight sides and corners. A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners. A rectangle has 4 sides and 4 corners.
sample.es: Los dos tienen lados rectos y esquinas. Un triángulo tiene 3 lados y 3 esquinas. Un rectángulo tiene 4 lados y 4 esquinas.

hints.en: Count the sides of each shape.
Count the corners of each shape.
Look for something that is the same and something that is not.

steps: Both shapes have straight sides and corners.
A triangle has 3 of each and a rectangle has 4 of each.
solution.es: Ambos tienen lados y esquinas; el triángulo tiene 3 y el rectángulo 4.

objective: Use composed shapes to count the parts in a pattern.

stem.es: 6 triángulos del mismo tamaño encajan para formar 1 hexágono. ¿Cuántos triángulos forman 2 hexágonos?

hints.en: One hexagon uses 6 triangles.
Two hexagons need two groups of 6.
Add 6 and 6.

objective: Decide which equation is true.

4 + 4 is 8, not 9.
5 + 2 is 7, not 8.

hints.en: Work out the side that has a plus sign.

objective: Sort equations into true and false.

stem.en: Sort each equation. Is it true or false?
stem.es: Clasifica cada ecuación. ¿Es verdadera o falsa?

If the amounts are the same, the equation is true.
Some equations have an addition on both sides.

solution.es: Son verdaderas las de lados iguales; 9 ≠ 10, 8 ≠ 9 y 9 ≠ 10 son falsas.

objective: Check which statements about a data set are true.

stem.en: The chart shows cats 4, dogs 7 and fish 2. Select ALL the true statements.
stem.es: La tabla muestra gatos 4, perros 7 y peces 2. Selecciona TODAS las afirmaciones verdaderas.

text.en: There are 3 more dogs than cats.

choices.why: Dogs and cats together make 7 + 4 = 11, not 10.

text.en: There are 3 more cats than fish.

choices.why: Cats are 4 and fish are 2, so there are 2 more cats than fish.

text.en: There are 5 more dogs than fish.

hints.en: Check each statement with the numbers in the chart.
Use subtraction for 'more' and addition for 'together'.
Three statements are true.

steps: 7 + 4 = 11 and 4 − 2 = 2 make the other two false.
solution.es: 7−4=3, 4+2=6 y 7−2=5 son verdaderas; las otras dos son falsas.

objective: Explain why changing the order of addends does not change the sum.

stem.en: Jin says 4 + 9 and 9 + 4 give different totals. Do you agree? Explain.
stem.es: Jin dice que 4 + 9 y 9 + 4 dan totales distintos. ¿Estás de acuerdo? Explica.

criteria.en: Says the totals are the same, 13
criteria.es: Dice que los totales son iguales, 13

criteria.en: Gives a reason such as the same groups put together
criteria.es: Da una razón, como que son los mismos grupos juntos

sample.en: I disagree. 4 + 9 = 13 and 9 + 4 = 13. The same two groups put together make the same total.
sample.es: No estoy de acuerdo. 4 + 9 = 13 y 9 + 4 = 13. Los mismos dos grupos juntos forman el mismo total.

hints.en: Work out both sums.
Draw a group of 4 and a group of 9.
Does it matter which group you count first?

steps: The same two groups make the same total.

objective: Match addition facts to their turn-around facts.

stem.en: Match each addition fact to its turn-around fact.
stem.es: Relaciona cada suma con la suma que tiene los números en otro orden.

Both facts in a pair have the same total.

solution.es: Cada pareja usa los mismos dos números en otro orden.

7 + 7 uses a different number, so the total changes.
Changing a 7 to a 5 makes the total smaller.

Does the order of the addends change the total?
Use the same two numbers, 7 and 5.

steps: Adding in a different order gives the same total.
solution.es: Cambiar el orden no cambia el total: 5 + 7 = 12.

n and 7 together make 12.

criteria.es: Dice que las dos clases tienen 10, así que ninguna tiene más
